prompt: The line $y = k$ intersects the graph of $y = x^2 - 6x + 5$ at exactly one point. What is the value of $k$?
hint: A horizontal line meets a parabola once only when it passes through the vertex.

hints.text: A horizontal line meets a parabola once only when it passes through the vertex.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try an easy parabola: $y = x^2$ meets $y = k$ once only when $k = 0$, the vertex height. A horizontal line touches a parabola exactly once precisely at the vertex.

learningObjective: Connect a single intersection with a horizontal line to the vertex of a parabola.
explanation: A horizontal line either misses an upward parabola, cuts it twice, or touches it exactly once — and the last case happens only at the vertex.

alternativeExplanations.title: Or force the discriminant to zero
steps: One solution means $36 - 4(5 - k) = 0$, giving $36 - 20 + 4k = 0$ and $k = -4$.
Both routes work; recognizing the vertex is faster, but the discriminant route generalizes to non-horizontal lines.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: x = 3, the vertex's input, is the classic wrong entry — the line y = k is horizontal, so k is a HEIGHT.
k must equal the vertex's y-value: f(3) = −4. Say which coordinate the question's object carries before answering.
